title: Affine-intersection vertical homology of the open Čech resolution
statement: Let X be separated, let i:X.Opens → X.Etale satisfy i followed by forgetting to schemes over X equals the restriction functor, and let U be any u-small family of affine opens (no covering or finiteness condition on the family). Let G be an étale abelian sheaf with values in universe u+1, assume injective resolutions exist, and assume positive derived evaluation of G vanishes on every affine étale X-scheme. For every injective resolution I of G and its actual double complex D defined in [def-sc-etale-open-cech-resolution-double-complex], the vertical-homology complex H^0_II(D) is isomorphic to C^bullet(U,i^*G). For each q>0 and each p, the object (H^q_II(D))^p is zero. No assertion about total homology or convergence is made.

proof.text: Evaluation of the Čech functor in degree p is restriction to the discrete tuple family followed by its product. Restriction preserves finite limits and colimits. Shrink Mathlib AB4StarOfSize for AddCommGrpCat from u+1 to u, so that this product is exact. The product-to-limit natural isomorphism therefore shows that this evaluation preserves homology. Map the short complex K.sc q through these functors and use NatTrans.app_homology for the Čech differentials. This constructs a complex isomorphism H^q_II(D) ≅ C^bullet(U,H^q(K)), where K is the resolution restricted to opens. All these steps are proved in Lean.

Sheaf-to-presheaf and restriction along i.op form a left exact additive functor A. Compose the inverse of I.isoRightDerivedObj A 0 with A.rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf to identify H^0(K) with A(G). Apply the Čech functor and compose the preceding complex isomorphism. This proves the bottom row.

The chosen product of a nonempty finite family of opens equals their infimum: the projections give one inequality and Pi.lift gives the other. Mathlib IsAffineOpen.iInf proves affineness of this intersection on a separated scheme. The functor equality identifies (i(V)).left with V as a scheme. The formula I.isoRightDerivedObj for evaluation transports hvan to homology of the evaluated resolution; evaluation preserves homology, so each value of H^q(K) at these products is zero. Product projection extensionality gives zero identity on each Čech term. The column isomorphism transports this vanishing. This includes empty tuple indexing and empty intersections; the proof is entirely Lean.
